$comment: The five tags GUML deliberately does not ship as builtins, provided as a registry package instead.
`chart`, `calendar`, `date`, `upload` and `command` were left out of the builtin vocabulary on a
specific argument, recorded in ROADMAP.md: no honest lowering exists without a design decision the
registry should not make for a host. A `chart` that emitted a bare `<div>` would be a promise the
compiler does not keep, and there is no neutral answer to 'which charting library' or 'which date
picker' — those belong to whoever is building the application.
A registry package is the answer to exactly that shape of problem, which is why this doubles as the
worked example `spec/REGISTRY.md` describes. Every entry uses a PascalCase `element` with an
`import`: the host owns the implementation, and the compiler emits `<Chart …>` plus the import rather
than trying to reimplement it. `src/index.tsx` is a small real implementation with no dependencies,
so the package is provable rather than illustrative.
Audit it with `guml registry --validate packages/guml-widgets`, install with `guml add`.
name: @guml/widgets

components.name: chart
components.doc: Chart of a resource. `of` is the row field to plot, `label` the field to name each point.

components.name: calendar
components.doc: Month grid. Bound state holds the selected ISO date.

components.name: date
components.doc: Single date input bound to a state holding an ISO date.

components.name: upload
components.doc: File picker. `accept` narrows the types; the action runs with the chosen files.

components.name: command
components.doc: Filterable command palette over a resource, shown while `if=` is true.
